\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Finite Law}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomVariables.FiniteLaw
\section{Overview}
Finite-support random variables have weighted-sum integral and norm formulas on arbitrary finite measure spaces. Two-point laws yield explicit centered moments and atom weights.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Integrating a finitely supported law]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteLaw.finite_law_integral}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $\mu$ be a finite measure, let $X:\Omega\to\bbr$ be measurable and supported almost everywhere on a finite set $s\subseteq\bbr$, and let $f:\bbr\to\bbr$ be arbitrary. Then $\int f(X)\,d\mu=\sum_{x\in s}\mu(X=x)f(x)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Affine norm for a finite law]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteLaw.finite_law_affine_norm_sq}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteLaw.finite_law_integral, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.HasAtomLowerBound, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.HasAtomLowerBound.memLp, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rvLpNorm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rvLpNorm_rpow}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\mu$ be a finite measure, let $X$ be measurable and supported almost everywhere on a finite $s\subseteq\bbr$, let $q>0$, and let $a,b\in\bbr$. Then $\|a+bX\|_q^2=(\sum_{x\in s}\mu(X=x)|a+bx|^q)^{2/q}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Two atoms carry the entire law]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteLaw.ae_two_point_of_mass_sum}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
Let $X$ be a measurable real random variable on a probability space and let $x\ne y$. If $\Pr[X=x]+\Pr[X=y]=1$, then $X\in\{x,y\}$ almost surely.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Affine norm for two points]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteLaw.two_point_affine_norm_sq}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteLaw.ae_two_point_of_mass_sum, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteLaw.finite_law_affine_norm_sq, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rvLpNorm}
\difficulty{4}
Let $X$ be measurable on a probability space, let $x\ne y$ and $0\le\lambda\le1$, and suppose $\Pr[X=x]=\lambda$ and $\Pr[X=y]=1-\lambda$. For $q>0$ and $a,b\in\bbr$, $\|a+bX\|_q^2=(\lambda|a+bx|^q+(1-\lambda)|a+by|^q)^{2/q}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Mean and variance of a centered Bernoulli law]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteLaw.centered_two_point_moments}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteLaw.ae_two_point_of_mass_sum, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteLaw.finite_law_integral, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteLaw.two_point_affine_norm_sq, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rvLpNorm}
\difficulty{4}
Let $X$ be measurable on a probability space and let $0\le\lambda\le1$. If $\Pr[X=1-\lambda]=\lambda$ and $\Pr[X=-\lambda]=1-\lambda$, then $\E X=0$ and $\|X\|_2^2=\lambda(1-\lambda)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Probability weights of finite atoms]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteLaw.finite_probability_atom_weights}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteLaw.finite_law_integral}
\difficulty{3}
Let $X$ be measurable on a probability space and supported almost surely on a finite set $s\subseteq\bbr$. If $\lambda\ge0$ and $\Pr[X=x]\ge\lambda$ for every $x\in s$, then the real atom weights $w_x=\Pr[X=x]$ satisfy $\sum_{x\in s}w_x=1$ and $w_x\ge\lambda$ for every $x\in s$.
\end{theorem}
